thread:
maria: heads-up — CI npm audit just flagged a HIGH vuln in ssri (<=9.0.1) coming in transitively via storybook deps. Noticed it on console/frontend build in CI. PR by dependabot: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/1234 :eyes:

dependabot: opened pull request #1234 to bump ssri to 9.0.2 in pnpm-lock.yaml (devDependency).

lee: is it only a devDependency? storybook often pulls ssri into build-time tooling, but ssri vuln can affect package extraction at runtime in some paths. we should assume potential prod exposure until we confirm.

sam: if it's only in devDeps, we probably won't need a prod hotfix, but agree we should triage quick. worried about lockfile churn if we upgrade storybook to force resolution.

maria: quick triage plan: 1) confirm transitive path (who pulls ssri) 2) try pnpm override to pin ssri 9.0.2 (minimal churn) 3) run full e2e + staging build 4) decide backport if needed.

jen: I can run the dependency tree in CI: `pnpm why ssri --recursive` and `pnpm audit --json | jq '.advisories'` — will post results in a minute.

jen: output snippet: ```
> pnpm why ssri
ssri@9.0.1
└─ @storybook/core@6.5.0 -> @mdx-js/loader@1.6.22 -> ssri@9.0.1
```

lee: ok so storybook pulls it in. that suggests dev-only, but still we don't want the vuln in our CI images (image reuse). prefer override.

sam: creating a pnpm-overrides PR is fine. does that avoid lockfile churn? It will update lockfile but not bump major storybook deps.

maria: exact override to propose: ```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "ssri": "9.0.2"
  }
}
```
we'll add to package.json in repo root, run `pnpm install` to regenerate pnpm-lock.yaml, then open a small PR.

lee: testing checklist: - smoke build local - CI integration job (build+storybook) - staging deploy with static assets - run `npm audit` in CI to ensure advisory cleared

taylor: do we need to backport to the stable branch (v1.3.x)? any customers on pinned versions?

sam: AFAIK only internal and a handful of early enterprise trials on dedicated infra. we should backport the override to release branch to be safe. small PR.

maria: timeline: if sam opens the PR today, QA can validate tomorrow, merge by EOD tomorrow if green. I'll schedule a brief canary deploy to staging after merge.

sam: will open PR now with the override + regenerated lockfile, and add the `# security` label.

dependabot: note — when merged, I will close the automated SSRI bump PR. audit-bot will run another sweep and post results.

audit-bot: automated audit run scheduled. will post results to this thread after merge. :robot_face:

lee: one more note — track the advisory CVE number in the PR and the security tracker (SEC-2026-1123) so we can reference in release notes and customer communication if needed.

maria: thanks everyone. keeping this minimal avoids wide churn. tagging @sam for follow-up. :thumbsup:

sam: got it — PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/1240 (pnpm override + lockfile) — assigning to @jen for CI runs.

jen: running CI now, will paste audit output when done.

jen: CI audit result: `0 vulnerabilities found` after applying override. staging build succeeded.

maria: merging & backporting to release branch now. will update SEC tracker after deploy.

maria: (post-merge) SEC-2026-1123 updated; release notes will include brief note about transitive dev-tool vuln and that customers are not impacted in production runtime.

lee: closing loop — add entry to eng-security playbook about prefer pnpm overrides for dev-toolchain transitive vulns to minimize churn.

sam: done — created follow-up doc in docs/patching/ssri-2026.md and linked in the PR. :white_check_mark:
